svg.aria-label: Interaction storyboard overview: eight frames of Sam using the site
svg.title: Interaction storyboard overview
svg.text: Interaction storyboard: Sam reads Beyond the Road Toll on a phone
Eight moments, 375px mobile view. Grey = structure, blue = controls, orange = Sam's touch and thoughts.

g.text: Fewer Australians are dying on the roads.
The number being seriously hurt hasn't fallen.
For every road death, 35 people were
Notes: Hospitalisations are people discharged alive...
Opens the link on the phone and scrolls
Headline, lede and unit chart: 1 dark
square for each road death, 35 grey for
The question is bigger than deaths: for
each person who dies, about 35 are
Per person, the rate has barely moved.
Notes: Per-person rates use ABS population at 30 June.
Lines re-index to 2011 = 100 per head; the
rising count line flattens and a read-out
Deaths fell, but per person the injury
rate has barely moved: it is not getting
Cycling injuries have more than doubled among over-65s.
Sentence rewrites itself for each pick.
Low-count cells (avg under 30 a year) are hatched.
Chooses 'I travel by: Pedal cyclist' and
'I'm aged: 40-64', then changes the age to
Own heatmap cell is outlined and a
sentence under the chart rewrites itself;
the earlier pick stays as a dashed ghost.
Older riders are the fast-growing group:
cyclists aged 75+ up 142%, and Sam sees
Tap a cell to see its line
the line shows whether it climbed steadily.
"Is it a blip, or a trend?"
The 2011-21 line for that cell appears
The rise is a sustained trend across the
decade, not a blip in the 3-year averages.
Pedestrian bar as Sam steps along:
Counts, not risk per trip: no data on how far people walk.
"Mum and Dad walk to the shops..."
Steps the measure: Admissions, then Bed
Bars switch to the chosen measure: the
admissions to 13.1% of bed days to 26.4%
of deaths; the label sits on the bar.
Pedestrians are few of the injured but
many of those who die: the risk for Sam's
walking parents is outcome, not frequency.
Cyclists: every month from April above the previous five years
The y-axis rescales between views, and the switch says so.
Switches All road users to Cyclists in the
The y-axis rescales; the 2020 line climbs
above the grey 2015-19 band and an
everything else fell: Sam's first year of
riding was a high-risk one for riders.
were hospitalised at about the same
rate. By 2021: half as high again.
Better recording of Indigenous status may
explain part of the rise. Counts alone hide
the gap because the population grew.
"Counts hid this. Per person it is clear."
Two lines separate (145 to 226 vs 149 to
149 per 100,000); a caveat box beside the
Counts hid a real gap: per person, First
as often again by 2021, with a caveat.
The road toll isn't the whole story.
If you ride, you're part of a growing group.
If your parents walk, it's what happens after.
The roads are not equally safe for everyone.
Scrolls sideways if wide; same data as the chart.
"Where does this come from? Let me check."
Opens 'Show the numbers' under a figure,
then reads the Methods and limitations
A text table with the chart's data
expands; the methods panel lists sources,
Sam can check the source (BITRE, ABS) and
knows the limits before sharing the story.
